q: An owner wants an entire neighborhood's zoning district changed from residential to commercial. In a New York town, which body has the power to amend the zoning ordinance and map?
options: The town board
The zoning board of appeals
The planning board
The building inspector
explanation: Adopting and amending zoning is a legislative act of the town board (city council or village board of trustees). The ZBA grants variances and interprets the ordinance; it cannot rezone.

q: In a New York village, which elected body adopts the zoning law and the village budget?
options: The zoning board of appeals
The planning board
The board of trustees
The board of assessment review
explanation: A village's legislative body is its board of trustees, which adopts local laws including zoning, plus the budget and tax rate. Appointed boards such as the planning board and ZBA do not.

q: Which statement about a town planning board is accurate?
options: Its members are elected by town voters, and it grants use and area variances
Its members are appointed by the town board, and it reviews subdivision plats
Its members are appointed by the governor, and it collects town property taxes
Its members are elected by town voters, and it adopts the annual town budget
explanation: Planning board members are appointed by the legislative body. The board performs authorized land-use review such as subdivision plats and site plans, and advises on the comprehensive plan.

q: A company wants to build an office building on a lot where offices are a permitted use. The town requires review of the parking layout, lighting, drainage and landscaping. This is:
options: A use variance hearing before the zoning board of appeals
A rezoning before the town board
A certificate of occupancy inspection
Site plan review, typically by the planning board
explanation: Site plan review examines how a permitted use is laid out on the parcel: parking, access, lighting, drainage and landscaping. No variance is needed because the use is allowed.

q: A building inspector denies a permit because he interprets a proposed garage apartment as a prohibited second dwelling. The owner believes the ordinance allows it. Where does the owner first appeal the interpretation?
options: The town board of assessment review
The County Clerk
The Department of State
The zoning board of appeals
explanation: The ZBA hears appeals from orders, interpretations and determinations of the administrative official charged with enforcing the zoning ordinance. It acts as the ordinance's interpreter.

q: Which description of a zoning board of appeals is most accurate?
options: A legislative body that rewrites the zoning map when owners request it
A quasi-judicial body that applies legal standards to appeals and variances
An elected body that sets the tax rate and adopts the budget
An advisory body whose decisions are never binding on applicants
explanation: The ZBA is administrative and quasi-judicial: it decides appeals, interpretations and variance requests under statutory standards. Rezoning is legislative and belongs to the governing board.

q: A property owner in a designated design district wants to replace a storefront facade and add a large sign. Which local body typically reviews exterior appearance, signs and fences where established?
options: The architectural review board
The board of assessment review
The conservation advisory council
The county health department
explanation: An architectural review board reviews the effect of new construction or alterations on the surrounding area, especially exteriors, signs and fences. Its approval is separate from zoning and building-code compliance.
citation: NY Town Law; NY Village Law (local architectural review law)

q: What is the primary role of a municipal conservation advisory council?
options: To issue building permits for new homes proposed near wetlands
To grant area and use variances for building in environmental zones
To study and advise on the community's natural resources and open space
To set assessed values for undeveloped open land on the tax roll
explanation: A conservation advisory council is an appointed body that inventories and advises on natural resources and open space. It does not issue building permits, grant variances, or replace a DEC wetland permit.

q: A buyer's agent wants to confirm that a finished basement was built with permits and passed inspection. Which local office should be contacted?
options: The building department or code enforcement office
The receiver of taxes or the town assessor's office
The zoning board of appeals or the planning board
The town board clerk's election office
explanation: The building department issues building permits, conducts inspections, issues certificates of occupancy/completion and handles violations. It is the gatekeeper for construction activity.
citation: NY Executive Law Article 18; local building code

q: A homeowner complains that her property tax bill is too high and asks who set the tax rate. Which statement is correct?
options: The assessor sets both the assessed value and the tax rate
The receiver of taxes sets both the assessed value and the tax rate
The assessor values property; the legislative body sets the levy and tax rate
The planning board sets the tax rate as part of the master plan
explanation: The assessor estimates value for the assessment roll. The governing body adopts the budget and tax levy, from which the rate is derived, and the receiver of taxes collects. These roles are separate.

q: A buyer is purchasing a rural lot with no public sewer. Which agency typically must approve the design of a new septic system?
options: The zoning board of appeals
The county health department
The architectural review board
The town assessor
explanation: Septic system design approval is typically handled by the county (or state) health department under sanitary code standards, not by zoning or design boards.
citation: NY Public Health Law; county sanitary code

q: A town proposes rezoning a parcel within 500 feet of a state highway. Before final action, New York law generally requires the town to:
options: Obtain approval from the State Department of Transportation
Hold a referendum of all town voters
Obtain a positive declaration under SEQR
Refer the proposal to the county planning agency for review
explanation: Certain zoning actions affecting property within 500 feet of a municipal boundary, state or county road, park or other listed facilities must be referred to the county planning agency. If the county recommends disapproval or modification, the local board can act contrary to it only by a vote of a majority plus one of all its members.

q: An owner of a designated landmark building in New York City wants to replace its original windows. Which agency must approve the work?
options: The Board of Standards and Appeals
The City Planning Commission
The local community board
The Landmarks Preservation Commission
explanation: NYC's Landmarks Preservation Commission designates landmarks and historic districts and regulates alterations to designated properties. Historic age alone is not landmark status.
citation: NYC Administrative Code § 25-301 et seq. (Landmarks Law)

q: In New York City, which agency issues building permits and certificates of occupancy and enforces the construction codes?
options: The City Planning Commission
The Department of Buildings
The Board of Standards and Appeals
The Department of Finance
explanation: The NYC Department of Buildings issues permits and COs, inspects work and enforces the construction codes and Zoning Resolution. CPC handles planning/zoning changes; BSA grants variances.
citation: NYC Charter Chapter 26; NYC Construction Codes

q: An owner in New York City needs a zoning variance for a building that cannot meet a setback requirement because of the lot's irregular shape. Which body decides the variance?
options: The Board of Standards and Appeals
The City Planning Commission
The NYC Department of Buildings
The local community board
explanation: In NYC, the Board of Standards and Appeals grants zoning variances and certain special permits and hears appeals from Department of Buildings determinations. It plays the role a ZBA plays elsewhere.

q: In New York City, which body votes on zoning map amendments during ULURP, after the community board and borough president have made recommendations?
options: The Board of Standards and Appeals
The Department of Buildings
The City Planning Commission
The Landmarks Preservation Commission
explanation: Under ULURP, the City Planning Commission holds a hearing and votes after the community board and borough president review. Its approvals then go to the City Council for review.

q: Which is the correct order of review under NYC's Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP) after an application is certified complete?
options: Community board, borough president, City Planning Commission, City Council
Borough president, community board, City Council, City Planning Commission
City Planning Commission, City Council, community board, borough president
Community board, City Council, borough president, City Planning Commission
explanation: ULURP runs: Department of City Planning certifies the application, then community board review, borough president review, City Planning Commission vote, and City Council review, with a possible mayoral veto.

q: Under ULURP, a community board votes to disapprove a proposed rezoning. What is the effect?
options: The application is automatically denied and may not proceed
The application must be refiled with the Board of Standards and Appeals
The recommendation is advisory; the application continues to later review stages
The rezoning may proceed only if the mayor overrides the board
explanation: Community board and borough president recommendations are advisory. Binding decisions are made by the City Planning Commission and the City Council.

q: Under ULURP, how long does the community board have to hold a public hearing and submit its recommendation after receiving a certified application?
options: 30 days
60 days
50 days
90 days
explanation: The community board has 60 days, the borough president 30 days, the City Planning Commission 60 days, and the City Council 50 days. Don't mix up the 30-day borough president period.

q: Before a town zoning board of appeals decides a variance application, Town Law requires the board to:
options: Obtain the town board's written consent
Get approval from the county clerk
Get a certificate of occupancy for the parcel
Hold a public hearing after giving public notice
explanation: The ZBA must fix a time for a public hearing, give public notice (including newspaper publication), and let interested parties be heard before deciding.

q: A neighbor believes the town ZBA wrongly granted a use variance next door. How is the decision generally challenged in court?
options: An Article 78 proceeding, which may be brought at any time within six years after the decision
An appeal to the town board, which may reverse any decision of the zoning board of appeals
A complaint to the Department of State, which may revoke the variance
An Article 78 proceeding, generally within 30 days after the decision is filed with the town clerk
explanation: ZBA decisions are reviewed by an Article 78 proceeding in State Supreme Court. Town Law sets a short deadline: 30 days after the decision is filed in the town clerk's office. The town board does not sit as an appeals body over the ZBA.

q: In an Article 78 proceeding challenging a planning board decision, what does the court generally decide?
options: Whether the court itself would have voted the same way after holding a new hearing
Whether the decision was illegal, arbitrary and capricious, or lacked a rational basis
Whether the applicant's project would be the most profitable use of the property
Whether a majority of residents support the planning board's decision
explanation: Article 78 review is deferential. The court asks whether the agency acted lawfully and rationally (not arbitrarily or capriciously) and does not substitute its own judgment or rehear the application from scratch.
